cases.rationale: Operative Specification 13 §9.3(ii) requires a qualifying registrant relationship; absence is explicitly declared rather than inferred from a Brand inventory flag.
The Registry Operator is an expressly allowed registrant alternative; current DNS setup is not required.
A qualifying Affiliate under the controlling agreement is an independent permitted class.
Specification13 §9.5 defines a qualifying legal-entity license for the google Brand trademark, with continuing substantive business use; no applicant-label-specific grant is required.
Specification13 §9.5 licenses the trademark corresponding to the Brand TLD string, not a literal candidate label; the same qualifying entity role applies while future-use policy remains a gap.
Specification13 §9.5 expressly requires a legal entity and excludes a person from the Trademark Licensee alternative.
A prospective domain need not already have DNS setup. §9.3(ii) restricts operational controllers to qualifying classes but does not make existing records a static eligibility prerequisite.
Missing facts cannot establish or disprove the allowed relationships; accepted name forms and other policy families remain unresearched.
A reviewed Google contract and Google-scoped declarations cannot supply a policy for another Brand namespace.
